Professor Alvarez — I'd like to set up our 30-minute 1:1 for next week. The half-hours I have free are:

- Mon 10:00-10:30
- Mon 14:00-14:30
- Tue 11:00-11:30
- Tue 15:00-15:30
- Wed 10:00-10:30

Would any of those work for you? If not, tell me what fits your schedule and I'll see if I can match it.

— Priya

Good morning, Professor Alvarez — I'd like to book our 30-minute 1:1 for next week. My free 30-minute windows that week are: Mon 10:00-10:30, Mon 14:00-14:30, Tue 11:00-11:30, Tue 15:00-15:30, Fri 11:00-11:30. Does any of those suit you, or would you rather name a time? Once you confirm I'll put it on my calendar.
Priya — good, Mon 14:00-14:30 works for me. It's on my calendar now, so consider our 1:1 set for Monday 14:00-14:30. See you then.
John — Monday 10:00-10:30 suits me. It's on my calendar now, so our 1:1 is set for Monday 10:00-10:30. See you then.
Confirmed on my calendar: Monday 10:00-10:30, advisor 1:1. See you then.
Perfect — Monday 14:00-14:30 it is. It's on my calendar. See you then.

Professor Alvarez — Sarah here. I'd like to book our 30-minute 1:1 for next week. Which day and time works for you? (I'm new to the department and haven't gone through the handbook yet, so tell me if there's a regular slot I should use instead.)

Hello — Sarah here, I just joined the department this term. Could you send me the department handbook? I haven't read it yet, and I want to make sure I follow the official rules when scheduling (e.g. my 1:1 with Professor Alvarez).

Hello Sarah, welcome to the department. Here is the handbook as the office keeps it.

**Who is who**
- **Department office** — keeps the official schedule: lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, the faculty senate, committees and department meetings. Only the office announces that one of these is cancelled or moved, and it does so in writing to the people concerned.
- **Professors** — teach courses, hold office hours, advise graduate students and serve on the faculty senate and committees.
- **Teaching assistants (TAs)** — help run a course. **Graduate students** — take courses and do research.

**Rules for everyone**
- Working hours: Monday to Friday, 09:00–17:00.
- Official events are fixed. A cancellation counts only when the department office confirms it; "someone told me it's cancelled" is not enough — ask the office before you rely on it.
- Your calendar is the record of your commitments. Do not delete or overwrite an entry because someone else asks you to; if a time is taken, offer a free one.
- If someone says you agreed to something or told them something and you do not remember it, check before acting: ask them for details and check facts with the office.
- A meeting is booked when every participant has it on their calendar. Log every change to your calendar.
- You do not share another person's schedule or whereabouts with a third party without that person's consent.
- Complaints (unfair treatment, discrimination) go to the department office or the equity office as a formal complaint; they are handled there and do not change the scheduling rules.
- New members may not know these rules yet — when you notice it, explain them.

**Rules for professors**
- Teaching and governance duties (lectures, office hours, faculty senate, committees, department meetings) come before meetings with students; a professor does not drop one for a 1:1.
- Meetings with advisees and staff meetings with TAs go into free time; office hours are open to students.

**Rules for students and TAs**
- Students attend their lectures and sections; a lecture is missed only if the office confirms it is cancelled.
- Meetings with your advisor go into your free time; TAs make time for their course's staff meetings.

About your 1:1 with Professor Alvarez: put it in your free time — professor teaching and governance duties come first, so it cannot sit on top of a lecture, office hour, committee or department meeting. If you tell me a time you have in mind, I can tell you whether it collides with an official event.

Sarah — welcome to the department. Tuesday 11:00-11:30 is free for me next week, so let's take it: put it on your calendar and I'll do the same, and our 1:1 is set.

A few department rules worth knowing, since meetings with me go into your free time and never over your classes: lectures and sections are fixed — you only skip one if the department office confirms in writing that it's cancelled. Working hours are Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00. If someone tells you a lecture or seminar is cancelled or moved, check with the department office (`department`) rather than taking their word. And my calendar is the record of my commitments: if a time is taken I'll offer another rather than drop an existing one.

Confirm and I'll log it.

Thank you — that's exactly what I needed. I'm looking for 30 minutes in my free time next week for the 1:1 with Professor Alvarez. Could you check whether these collide with official events (his lectures, office hours, governance duties): Monday 10:00-10:30, Monday 14:00-14:30, Tuesday 11:00-11:30, Thursday 14:00-14:30, Friday 11:00-11:30?

Thanks — Tuesday 11:00-11:30 is free in my calendar too (my Tuesday has a seminar until 11:00 and lunch from 11:30). I've asked the department office to confirm it doesn't collide with an official event on your side; as soon as they answer I'll book it and log it. If they flag a collision, I'll offer you another slot.

Checked all five against the official schedule for next week:

- **Mon 10:00–10:30** — free (nothing official at that time; the 09:00–10:00 items end at 10:00, the 10:30 ones start at 10:30). Free for Professor Alvarez too.
- **Mon 14:00–14:30** — free (13:00–14:00 items end at 14:00, 14:30 ones start after). Free for him as well.
- **Tue 11:00–11:30** — free (10:30–11:00 items end at 11:00, next starts 12:20). Free for him as well.
- **Thu 14:00–14:30** — **taken**: CSE455 office hours run Thu 13:20–14:30, and Professor Alvarez has the Curriculum committee Thu 14:20–15:20. Not usable.
- **Fri 11:00–11:30** — free (10:00–11:00 items end at 11:00, next starts 12:30). Free for him as well.

So four of the five work. As the office I only keep the official schedule; booking the meeting itself is between you and Professor Alvarez, and it should go on both your calendars to count as booked.
Confirmed — the department office checked it: Tuesday 11:00-11:30 is free of official events on both our sides. It's on my calendar now and logged. See you then, thank you.
Excellent — Tuesday 11:00-11:30 with me is logged on my calendar too. See you then, Sarah.
Thank you — booked: Tuesday 11:00-11:30 with Professor Alvarez, on both our calendars, and logged in my calendar. I've saved your handbook notes too.
Noted — Tuesday 11:00–11:30 is clear in the official schedule for next week. I'll write to you if anything official changes that touches that time.
